verses.1: Saulus, however, was pleased with his being dismissed from his position. On that day, great persecution occurred against the church in Jerusalem. All of them scattered across the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.
verses.2: Then, the honest men cut down the tree, and they made a large pole from it.
verses.3: Saul, however, was trying to organize the church by going from house to house, taking men and women and bringing them into prison.
verses.4: So, those who were scattered went out to spread the word.
verses.5: But when Philip arrived in the city of Samaria, he proclaimed to them the message of Christ.
verses.6: The crowd, however, paid attention to those who were considered followers of Philip. They listened to them and observed the signs he made.
verses.7: For many of those who were affected by this evil spirit, it was cured through loud shouting. Many others, however, who were also affected, were healed.
verses.8: Many blessings came to that city as a result.
verses.9: There was also a man named Simon who lived in that city. He was a magician and he controlled the people of Samaria. He claimed to be very great in his own eyes.
verses.10: Everyone tried to get ahead, from the smallest to the biggest. This is the Power of God, known as the Great One.
verses.11: And they were brought forth from those magics at the proper time.
verses.12: And when they believed in Philip’s preaching about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
verses.13: And Simon also believed in it. After being baptized by Philip, he became a follower of Christ. He saw that there were great signs and powers being manifested through him.
verses.14: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
verses.15: So that, after they have ascended, they may receive the holy breath.
verses.16: For they had no one to lead them; only those who were baptized entered into the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.17: Then they placed their hands on them, and received a holy breath.
verses.18: And seeing that through the attacks of the apostles’ hands, they were able to gain money for them.
verses.19: He said, “Give me this authority, so that when I place my hands on them, I may receive the Holy Spirit.”
verses.20: But Peter said to him, “Your gold and silver goods are of no use to you if you waste the gift of God by using money instead.”
verses.21: It’s not your fault either; there’s no harm in this statement. After all, your heart isn’t truly loyal to God.
verses.22: Let us then be freed from your evil ways. And ask the Lord whether it is truly right for you to give up your heart’s desires.
verses.23: For I see you as being trapped in bitterness and injustice.
verses.24: Then Simon replied, “Please do something for me before you go to the Lord. Please ensure that nothing bad happens to me as a result of your actions.”
verses.25: Those who were protesting and speaking out against the words of the Lord, they went to Jerusalem. There, they preached the message of the Lord to many people from Samaria.
verses.26: The angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Take up your cross and follow me. Go along the road that leads from Jerusalem to Gaza. That is the way to go.”
verses.27: And he went out into the streets. There he saw a man named Eithiopus, a brave warrior who was under the rule of King Candace of Eithiopia. He was very popular among his people. He gathered people to worship in Jerusalem.
verses.28: He was also standing below, sitting on his horse, and he recognized the prophet Esaias.
verses.29: And the Spirit said to Philip, “Come and be attached to this chariot.”
verses.30: Then Philip, after hearing about the deeds of Isaiah as a prophet, said, “Do you really think that what you’re doing is right?”
verses.31: And he said, “How can I possibly go anywhere if no one guides me?” He then asked Philip to sit down with him.
verses.32: The region where this writing was created was like this: It was like a sheep being led to the slaughterhouse. It remained closed, just as if it were silent in contrast to what was happening around it. In the same way, its “mouth” remains closed.
verses.33: In his humility, his judgment was made. Who can tell us about his origin? That his life is rejected by the earth.
verses.34: Then the hypocrite replied to Philip, “I wonder, what does the prophet mean by this? Does he mean about himself, or about someone else?”
verses.35: And when Philip opened his mouth, and began to preach from this scripture, Jesus came to him.
verses.36: As they traveled along the road, they came upon some water. The eunuch said, “Look, there’s water here. Why don’t I get baptized in it?”
verses.38: And he ordered that the chariot be prepared. Both of them went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch. He then bathed him in that water.
verses.39: But when they climbed out of the water, the Lord’s spirit took Philip away. He no longer recognized him as a faithful follower; instead, he continued to walk along that path, rejoicing in his journey.
verses.40: Philip was found in Azotus. He went there and proclaimed the good news to all the cities, until he arrived in Cæsarea.
